grades.quote: The LW instruction loads a 32-bit value from memory and sign-extends this to 64 bits before storing it in register _rd_ for RV64I. The LWU instruction, on the other hand, zero-extends the 32-bit value from memory for RV64I. LH and LHU are defined analogously for 16-bit values, as are LB and LBU for 8-bit values.
grades.reason: Directly establishes that LB sign-extends while LBU zero-extends: when bit 7 is 1, upper register bits become ones versus zeros.
